args.prompt:
Create a native game sprite atlas with EXACTLY THIRTY-TWO NEW complete full-body drawings of ONE named adult character, FOUR equal columns by EIGHT full rows on a tall portrait transparent RGBA canvas. Detailed crisp pixel-art adult proportions, same character and outfit in every cell. No text, numbers, grid, borders, scenery, painted floor or cast-shadow disks. Every body AND all held equipment has generous12–15% transparent cell margins: complete hair, hands, arms, legs, boot soles and weapon tips; never crop last-row feet. Same shared BODY DRAWING SCALE throughout the source; crouches/kneels remain naturally shorter, not inflated. Side/three-quarter facing RIGHT.
IDENTITY/VERSION: Ellis, Left4Dead2 game2009: young ADULT white male mechanic, short brown hair under BLUE-and-WHITE baseball/trucker cap, yellow short-sleeved mechanic T-shirt with a small simple dark chest emblem, blue jeans, brown belt and work shoes/boots. Slim wiry human body, no infected form. No giant grenade launcher permanently held.
EQUIPMENT/ROLE: Selected BASIC firearm is a compact real black UZI-style SMG with box magazine and short barrel, carried low/on sling outside basic firing. SUPPORT special uses a small physical metal spanner and compact closed toolkit, inspecting equipment and signalling readiness. No whole vehicle, turret, rocket/cannon, magic repair ray or helicopter in body cells.
Attached OLD atlas is an appearance cue only. Redraw every pose; correct equipment and role according to the text above. Never copy old offensive effects into a support action.
EIGHT DISTINCT STORYBOARD ROWS, FOUR anatomical poses each, top to bottom:
ROW 1: INTRO (1) stand with SMG slung low, (2) tip blue/white cap brim with free hand, (3) check small spanner in belt pouch, (4) alert ready stance with gear held safely down.
ROW 2: OUTRO (1) lower spanner after checking gear, (2) place it into compact toolkit, (3) close toolkit and secure it at belt, (4) turn away with a small cheerful follow signal.
ROW 3: ROUND VICTORY (1) breathe out and lower shoulders, (2) wipe forehead with sleeve, (3) short confident thumbs-up, (4) relaxed ready stance with weapon inactive.
ROW 4: ROUND DEFEAT alive and regrouping: (1) recoil with free forearm guarding and knees bent, (2) low bent-knee crouch with equipment safely controlled, (3) one knee down with head lowered and free hand bracing if available, (4) rise halfway looking toward fight. No injury, blood, death or lost equipment.
ROW 5: FINALE ADAPTATION BUFF SUPPORT equipment readiness: (1) crouch with small toolkit open beside boot, (2) one knee down inspecting a compact mechanical component held in palm with spanner, (3) rise halfway and tighten/check that component with real tool, (4) stand and offer confirming thumbs-up with equipment inactive. No magic beam, vehicle summon, enemy or execution.
ROW 6: MATCH VICTORY (1) close compact toolkit, (2) put spanner back at belt, (3) tip cap and small satisfied grin, (4) turn shoulders away with open-palm team signal.
ROW 7: MATCH DEFEAT alive fatigue: (1) shoulders sag with equipment safely down, (2) sink to one knee with free palm on thigh if available, (3) rest on heel head lowered with all held objects still physically supported, (4) lift head and brace to rise, both complete feet visible. No corpse, wounds, blood or dropped/disconnected anatomy.
ROW 8: SUPER BUFF SUPPORT: (1) kneel and set compact toolkit beside boot, (2) lean over real spanner and small mechanical component in left palm, (3) stand halfway checking the component with different elbows/legs, (4) upright thumbs-up and tool safely lowered. Four real body poses; no firing or supernatural repair light.
Final check: EIGHT full rows x FOUR complete bodies=32. Four distinct shoulder/elbow/torso/leg drawings per row, not glow-only recolors. Physical weapon emitters point RIGHT in aiming/recoil columns2 and3 of damaging super/finale rows; columns1 and4 are lowered preparation/recovery with no emission. Support actions never fire weapons. Long beams, projectiles, magical barriers and target explosions belong to runtime, never paint them across body cells. No victim, gore, execution, injured body, transformation or extra person.

outputHint:
Generated images are saved to /workspace/generated_images as /workspace/generated_images/exec-19a8e1ea-7567-4bd4-98bc-4b18e44705d7.png by default.
If you need to use a generated image at another path, copy it and leave the original in place unless the user explicitly asks you to delete it.
The generated image is already displayed to the user. There is no need to render it in the final response as a Markdown image or file link.
